sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Today we're going to be looking at animals in urban environments and I'm going to be telling you about some research on how they're affected by these environments.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将探讨城市环境中的动物，我将向大家介绍一些关于这些动物如何受到这些环境影响的研究。

sentences.en: Now, in evolutionary terms, urban environments represent huge upheavals, the sorts of massive changes that usually happen over millions of years.
sentences.zh: 从进化论的角度来看，城市环境代表着巨大的剧变，这类巨变通常需要数百万年才能发生。

sentences.en: And we used to think that only a few species could adapt to this new environment.
sentences.zh: 过去我们曾认为，只有少数物种能够适应这种新环境。

sentences.en: One species which is well known as being.
sentences.zh: 其中一种以高度适应性而闻名的物种是乌鸦，

sentences.en: highly adaptable is the crow, and there've been various studies about how they manage to learn new skills.
sentences.zh: 已有各种研究探讨它们如何学会新技能。

sentences.en: Another successful species is the pigeon, because they're able to perch on ledges on the walls of city buildings, just like they once perched on cliffs by the sea.
sentences.zh: 另一种成功的物种是鸽子，因为它们能在城市建筑墙壁的壁架上栖息，就像它们过去在海边悬崖上栖息一样。

sentences.en: But in fact, we're now finding that these early immigrants were just the start of a more general movement of animals into cities, and of adaptation by these animals to city life.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我们现在发现，这些早期的‘移民’只是动物大规模进入城市以及适应城市生活的更普遍趋势的开端。

sentences.en: And one thing that researchers are finding especially interesting is the speed with which they're doing this - we're not talking about gradual evolution here - these animals are changing fast.
sentences.zh: 研究人员尤其感兴趣的一点是它们完成这一适应过程的速度——我们谈论的并非渐进式的进化，而是这些动物正在迅速发生变化。

sentences.en: Let me tell you about some of the studies that have been carried out in this area.
sentences.zh: 让我为大家介绍一些在该领域开展的研究。

sentences.en: So, in the University of Minnesota, a biologist called Emilie Snell-Rood and her colleagues looked at specimens of urbanised small mammals such as mice and gophers that had been collected in Minnesota, and that are now kept in museums there.
sentences.zh: 例如，在明尼苏达大学，生物学家艾米莉·斯内尔-罗德（Emilie Snell-Rood）及其同事考察了在明尼苏达州采集的、已城市化的啮齿类小哺乳动物（如老鼠和囊鼠）标本，这些标本目前保存在当地博物馆中。

sentences.en: And she looked at specimens that had been collected over the last hundred years, which is very short time in evolutionary terms.
sentences.zh: 她考察的是过去一百年间采集的标本，而从进化角度看，这时间非常短暂。

sentences.en: And she found that during that time, these small mammals had experienced a jump in brain size when compared to rural mammals.
sentences.zh: 她发现，在此期间，与乡村哺乳动物相比，这些小型哺乳动物的脑容量显著增加。

sentences.en: Now, we can't be sure this means they're more intelligent, but since the sizes of other parts of the body didn't change, it does suggest that something cognitive was going on.
sentences.zh: 我们尚不能确定这意味着它们更聪明，但由于身体其他部分的尺寸并未发生变化，这确实表明某种认知层面的变化正在发生。

sentences.en: And Snell-Rood thinks that this change might reflect the cognitive demands of adjusting to city life - having to look in different places to find food, for example, and coping with a whole new set of dangers.
sentences.zh: 斯内尔-罗德认为，这种变化可能反映了适应城市生活所带来的认知需求——例如，需要在不同地点寻找食物，以及应对一整套全新的危险。

sentences.en: Then over in Germany at the Max Planck Institute, there's another biologist called Catarina Miranda who's done some experiments with blackbirds living in urban and rural areas.
sentences.zh: 而在德国马克斯·普朗克研究所，另一位生物学家卡塔琳娜·米兰达（Catarina Miranda）则对生活在城市和乡村地区的黑鸟开展了实验。

sentences.en: And she's been looking not at their anatomy but at their behaviour.
sentences.zh: 她关注的并非其解剖结构，而是其行为表现。

sentences.en: So as you might expect, she's found that the urban blackbirds tend to be quite bold - they're prepared to face up to a lot of threats that would frighten away their country counterparts.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如你所预料的那样，她发现城市黑鸟往往相当大胆——它们敢于直面许多会让乡村同类惊慌逃窜的威胁。

sentences.en: But there's one type of situation.
sentences.zh: 但有一种情况

sentences.en: that does seem to frighten the urban blackbirds, and that's anything new - anything they haven't experienced before.
sentences.zh: 似乎的确会让城市黑鸟感到恐惧，那就是任何新事物——任何它们此前未曾经历过的状况。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, that's quite sensible for a bird iving in the city.
sentences.zh: 仔细想来，这对一只生活在城市里的鸟而言其实相当合理。

sentences.en: Jonathan Atwell, in Indiana University, is looking at how a range of animals respond to urban environments.
sentences.zh: 印第安纳大学的乔纳森·阿特韦尔（Jonathan Atwell）正在研究一系列动物对城市环境的反应。

sentences.en: He's found that when they're under stress, their endocrine systems react by reducing the amount of hormones such as corticosterone into their blood.
sentences.zh: 他发现，当它们处于压力之下时，其内分泌系统会通过减少血液中皮质酮等激素的分泌量来作出反应。

sentences.en: It's a sensible- seeming adaptation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种看似合理的适应机制。

sentences.en: A rat that gets scared every time a subway train rolls past won't be very successful.
sentences.zh: 一只每次地铁列车驶过就吓得魂飞魄散的老鼠，恐怕很难生存成功。

sentences.en: There's just one more study I'd like to mention which is by Sarah Partan and her team, and they've been looking at how squirrels communicate in an urban environment, and they've found that a routine part of their communication is carried out by waving their tails.
sentences.zh: 我还想提一下由萨拉·帕坦（Sarah Partan）及其团队开展的另一项研究，他们一直在观察松鼠在城市环境中如何交流，并发现摇摆尾巴是其日常交流中一个常规组成部分。

sentences.en: You do also see this in the country, but it's much more prevalent in cities, possibly because it's effective in a noisy environment.
sentences.zh: 你在乡村地区也能看到这种行为，但在城市中却更为普遍，这或许是因为在嘈杂环境中这种方式更为有效。

sentences.en: So what are the long-term implications of this?
sentences.zh: 那么，这会产生哪些长期影响呢？

sentences.en: One possibility is that we may see completely new species developing in cities.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是，我们或许会在城市中见证全新物种的诞生。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, it's possible that not all of these adaptations will be permanent.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，也有可能并非所有这些适应性变化都会永久保留下来。

sentences.en: Once the animal's got accustomed to its new environment, it may no longer need the features it's developed.
sentences.zh: 一旦动物已完全适应其新环境，它可能就不再需要自己发展出的那些特征了。

sentences.en: So, now we've had a look ...
sentences.zh: 那么，现在我们已经了解……
